title: 5.7.22 Challenges
description: Pick one (or more) OOP stretch challenges: extend your Enemy class, write a Player class, or try subclassing with `extends`. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Define a class
steps.instructions: Declare at least one class using the `class` keyword.
hints: Re-read 5.6.3 Reading for the `class Name { ... }` shape.

steps.title: Instantiate the class
steps.instructions: Build an instance with `new ClassName(...)` and store it in a variable.
hints: 5.6.7 Worked Example shows `new Sprite(...)`: the same pattern applies to your own class.

steps.title: Write a constructor
steps.instructions: Give the class a `constructor(...)` that stores its arguments on `this`.
hints: 5.6.3 Reading walks through the three parts of a class: constructor, `this`, and methods.

steps.title: Use one OOP feature
steps.instructions:
Pick one of the challenges below and build it using at least one of: `this.<property>` access, `extends` another class, or a `super(...)` call.

**Challenge 1: isAlive (easy).** Write `class Enemy` whose constructor stores `x`, `y` and `hp` on `this`, with an `isAlive()` method that returns `this.hp > 0`. Build one with `new Enemy(...)` and check `enemy.isAlive()` in `draw()`.

**Challenge 2: a Player class (medium).** Write `class Player` whose constructor makes a sprite and stores it on `this.sprite`. Give it a `move(dir)` method that sets `this.sprite.vel.x` (negative for `'left'`, positive for `'right'`) and a `jump()` method that sets `this.sprite.vel.y` to a negative number. Build one with `new Player(200, 200)` and call `player.move('left')` or `player.jump()` from `draw()`.

**Challenge 3: a PowerUp subclass (hard).** Write `class Collectible` whose constructor stores `x`, `y`, `value` and `color` on `this`. Then write `class PowerUp extends Collectible` (the `extends` from 5.7.21): its constructor takes the same four arguments and must call `super(x, y, value, color);` first, which runs the parent's constructor, before it touches `this`. Add a `boost()` method that returns `this.value * 2`, and build one with `new PowerUp(100, 100, 10, 'gold')`.
hints: All three challenges pass the check with `this.` alone; `extends` and `super(` count too.
5.7.11 (Worked Example: Write an Enemy class (integration)) builds a class with a constructor, `this.sprite` and methods: the same shape works for every challenge.
